interactive.title: Simplify 6/8 to Lowest Terms
interactive.instructions: Enter 6/8 as a reduced fraction in lowest terms.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Reduce fraction six eighths to lowest terms
interactive.fallbackText: Divide numerator and denominator by their highest common factor 2: 6/8 = 3/4.

interactive.title: Round 9.995 to 2 Decimal Places
interactive.instructions: Enter 9.995 rounded to exactly 2 decimal places (half-up). Keep trailing zeros.
interactive.fallbackText: The third decimal digit is 5, so 9.995 rounds up with carry-over to 10.00.
interactive.successExplanation: Exact BigInt decimal arithmetic avoids binary float drift: 9.995 -> 10.00.

interactive.title: Simplify (x² − 9) / (x − 3) and State Domain Restriction
interactive.instructions: Enter the simplified expression and state the excluded value of x from the original denominator.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Simplify x squared minus 9 over x minus 3 with domain restriction
interactive.fallbackText: (x² − 9)/(x − 3) = x + 3, with x ≠ 3 because the original denominator vanishes at x = 3.
interactive.successExplanation: Cancelling (x − 3) removes the factor algebraically, but x ≠ 3 remains excluded from the original domain.

interactive.title: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0
interactive.instructions: Enter ALL real roots separated by a comma (e.g. 2, 3).
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Find all roots of x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0
interactive.fallbackText: (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, so the complete solution set is {2, 3}.
interactive.successExplanation: Both x = 2 and x = 3 satisfy the quadratic.

interactive.title: Solve √(x + 2) = x
interactive.instructions: Solve √(x + 2) = x and enter ONLY valid real roots that satisfy the original equation.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Solve square root of x plus 2 equals x
interactive.fallbackText: Squaring gives x² − x − 2 = 0 -> x = 2 or x = −1. Checking in the original equation: √(2+2)=2 (valid), √(−1+2)=1 ≠ −1 (extraneous). Only x = 2 is valid.
interactive.successExplanation: x = −1 is extraneous because the principal square root is non-negative.

interactive.title: Combine ln(x) + ln(x − 2) and State Domain
interactive.instructions: Write ln(x) + ln(x − 2) as a single logarithm and state the valid domain for x.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Combine natural log of x plus natural log of x minus 2 with domain
interactive.fallbackText: ln(x) + ln(x − 2) = ln(x(x − 2)) for x > 2 (both x > 0 and x − 2 > 0 must hold).
interactive.successExplanation: Although x(x − 2) > 0 also holds for x < 0, the original expression requires both x > 0 and x > 2, so x > 2.
